title: Traction Threads: weekly lab & metric experiments
content:
Notes to self (quick hit)

Context: this is my personal, weekly scratchpad for tracking small experiments that should move my personal output and the little funnels I own (demo->trial->setup conversations). Not a formal OKR doc — more like 1) micro-experiments, 2) leading indicators, 3) quick retros and next actions.

Top outcomes I care about this week
- Demo-to-trial conversions: moving from ~9% -> target 15% over 6 weeks (focus on follow-up email A/B)
- Shorten demo booking to fulfillment time from avg 4 days -> target 48 hours
- 2 small automation experiments to remove manual steps in onboarding guide

Metrics snapshot (last 3 weeks)
- Week of 2026-02-03: demos booked 12, trials started 1, conv 8.3%
- Week of 2026-02-10: demos booked 15, trials started 2, conv 13.3%
- Week of 2026-02-17: demos booked 11, trials started 1, conv 9.1%
- Running 6-week goal: ramp to 15% conv by 2026-03-31

Leading indicators I’ll watch daily
- # of demo reminders sent within 24h of booking (goal: 100%)
- Follow-up email open rate (goal: 35%+ for first week)
- Time from demo->trial invite sent (goal: median <24h)

Hypotheses & experiments (current)
1) Demo follow-up copy variant (A vs. B)
  - Hypothesis: Variant B (short checklist + next steps) reduces friction and increases trial starts by +50% vs baseline.
  - Launch: 2026-02-14
  - Measure: trial starts within 7 days of demo; also open rate and reply rate.
  - Status: rolling; early signal shows open rate +12% (n small).

2) Auto-send trial invite via workflow (remove manual step)
  - Hypothesis: automating invite reduces demo->trial latency and avoids drop-off.
  - Implementation: Zapier -> internal API (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/playbooks/pull/88).
  - Risk: invite rate might feel impersonal -> monitor replies.

3) 48h sprint on onboarding doc clarity (shorten checklist, add GIF)
  - Hypothesis: clearer onboarding reduces support-touch and increases trial activation rate.
  - Quick test: replace section 'first run' with 3-step GIF and measure activation rate.

Personal productivity experiments (micro)
- 90-min deep work blocks before lunch (goal: 5x/week). Status: 3/5 this week.
- 2x weekly syncs with Maya (30m) to unblock growth experiments — schedule recurring.

Quick log (captures partial thoughts)
- 2026-02-12 AM: brainstormed follow-up copy with Maya. She suggested 2 CTAs (start trial / book help). Might be confusing — test both but track which CTA clicked.
- 2026-02-13 PM: deployed variant B to 30% of demos (via campaign tool). Buddy Rafi helped instrument tracking (Jira PROJ-GROWTH-342).
- 2026-02-16: early signal: replies up, but trial starts only ticked +1. Need to check invite friction.

Retrospective (mini)
- What went well: quick rollout of follow-up copy; tracking worked end-to-end; small lift in engagement.
- What didn’t: invited users sometimes never received trial invite because of a manual step I missed. That leak costs us ~1-2 conversions/week.
- Insights: Little process frictions compound — prioritize automating the invite. Also need clearer measurement for "trial started" (some people set up but never accept email).

Open questions / To-dos
- [ ] Confirm final event that counts as "trial started" (analytics team/Confluence page mismatch). See linked Confluence page for definitions.
- [ ] Follow up with Rafi to finalize Zap -> internal API mapping and test on staging. (PR linked above)
- [ ] Add CTA click tracking to follow-up email (track both 'start trial' and 'book help').
- [ ] Create short onboarding GIF (ask Product Designer to reuse existing assets) — aim to ship by 2026-02-22.
- [ ] Schedule weekly 30m sync with Maya (recurring).

Risks / things to watch
- If auto-invite has too many bounce/errors, might harm deliverability. Add bounce monitoring and fallback policy to manual send.
- Over-testing small copy with tiny n leads to noise — keep minimum sample size per variant (n >= 40 demos) before deciding.

Notes & links (for quick reference)
- Confluence: onboarding event definitions -> https://confluence.redwood.com/pages/viewpage.action?pageId=987654321
- Jira: tracking issue -> PROD-GROWTH-342
- GitHub: automation PR -> https://github.com/redwood-inference/playbooks/pull/88
- Slack: growth thread -> #growth-thread (link above)

Reflection (end of week)
- Small wins matter: moved follow-ups faster which nudged engagement up. Biggest leverage is removing manual handoffs. Next week the goal is to close that automation gap and then re-run the email A/B with a clean funnel.

If I only do three things next week:
1) Ship the Zap->API test and validate on staging.
2) Finish onboarding GIF and replace current doc.
3) Ensure CTA tracking is in place and re-run the A/B with n >= 40 before calling it.

Quick reminders to self:
- Log measurement changes in Confluence before toggling event names.
- Keep Slack notes concise when asking for help; include exact repro steps.
- Block morning deep work and protect calendar from 10:30–12:00 daily.

End of note.

— Lucas
